sanskrit: eṣa raudraś ca saṃghāto mahān yuktaś ca tejasā somasya vahnisūryābhyām adbhuto 'yaṃ samāgamaḥ janayed yaṃ sutaṃ somaḥ so 'syā devyāḥ patir bhavet
english: This fierce conjunction is great and charged with radiance — a wondrous meeting of Soma, Fire, and Sun. Whichever son Soma might beget from this, he shall become the husband of this goddess.

sanskrit: agniś caitair guṇair yuktaḥ sarvair agniś ca devatā eṣa cej janayed garbhaṃ so 'syā devyāḥ patir bhavet
english: Agni, endowed with all these qualities, is himself a deity. If he should father a child, that son shall be the husband of this goddess.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃcintya bhagavān brahmalokaṃ tadā gataḥ gṛhītvā devasenāṃ tām avandat sa pitāmaham uvāca cāsyā devyās tvaṃ sādhu śūraṃ patiṃ diśa
english: Having thus reflected, the blessed Indra went then to the world of Brahmā. Taking Devasena with him, he bowed before the Grandfather and said: 'Be gracious — bestow on this goddess a valiant husband.'

sanskrit: brahmovāca yathaitac cintitaṃ kāryaṃ tvayā dānavasūdana tathā sa bhavitā garbho balavān uruvikramaḥ
english: Brahmā said: 'O slayer of demons, even as you have pondered this matter, so shall it be — a mighty womb shall bring forth a son of vast heroism.'

sanskrit: sa bhaviṣyati senānīs tvayā saha śatakrato asyā devyāḥ patiś caiva sa bhaviṣyati vīryavān
english: 'He shall become the commander of your armies, O Indra of a hundred sacrifices, and he shall become the brave husband of this goddess.'

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca etac chrutvā namas tasmai kṛtvāsau saha kanyayā tatrābhyagacchad devendro yatra devarṣayo 'bhavan vasiṣṭhapramukhā mukhyā viprendrāḥ sumahāvratāḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Hearing this, Indra bowed to Brahmā and departed with the maiden to the place where the divine sages dwelt — foremost among them Vasiṣṭha, the greatest among brahmin seers, all of mighty vows.

sanskrit: bhāgārthaṃ tapasopāttaṃ teṣāṃ somaṃ tathādhvare pipāsavo yayur devāḥ śatakratupurogamāḥ
english: Thirsting for the soma those sages had earned through austerity at their sacrifice, the gods went there with Indra leading the way.

sanskrit: iṣṭiṃ kṛtvā yathānyāyaṃ susamiddhe hutāśane juhuvus te mahātmāno havyaṃ sarvadivaukasām
english: Having performed the rite as prescribed, into the well-kindled fire those great-souled sages poured oblations on behalf of all the dwellers in heaven.

sanskrit: samāhūto hutavahaḥ so 'dbhutaḥ sūryamaṇḍalāt viniḥsṛtyāyayau vahnir vāgyato vidhivat prabhuḥ āgamyāhavanīyaṃ vai tair dvijair mantrato hutam
english: Summoned, the wondrous fire-bearer emerged from the solar disc and came forth — the mighty lord, his speech restrained, as prescribed by rule — and approached the offering fire into which those twice-born had poured oblations with mantras.

sanskrit: sa tatra vividhaṃ havyaṃ pratigṛhya hutāśanaḥ ṛṣibhyo bharataśreṣṭha prāyacchata divaukasām
english: There the fire-devourer received the various oblations, O best of the Bhāratas, and conveyed them to the heaven-dwellers on behalf of the sages.

sanskrit: niṣkrāmaṃś cāpy apaśyat sa patnīs teṣāṃ mahātmanām sveṣv āśrameṣūpaviṣṭāḥ snāyantīś ca yathāsukham
english: As he came out, he also saw the wives of those great-souled sages seated in their own hermitages and bathing at their ease.

sanskrit: rukmavedinibhās tās tu candralekhā ivāmalāḥ hutāśanārcipratimāḥ sarvās tārā ivādbhutāḥ
english: They were like golden altar-pedestals, pure as crescent moons, resembling the flames of the sacrificial fire, all of them wondrous as stars.

sanskrit: sa tadgatena manasā babhūva kṣubhitendriyaḥ patnīr dṛṣṭvā dvijendrāṇāṃ vahniḥ kāmavaśaṃ yayau
english: His mind fixed upon them, his senses became agitated; beholding the wives of those foremost brahmins, Fire fell under the sway of desire.

sanskrit: sa bhūyaś cintayām āsa na nyāyyaṃ kṣubhito 'smi yat sādhvīḥ patnīr dvijendrāṇām akāmāḥ kāmayāmy aham
english: He reflected again: 'It is not right that I, agitated as I am, should desire the chaste wives of those great brahmins — women who do not desire me.'

sanskrit: naitāḥ śakyā mayā draṣṭuṃ spraṣṭuṃ vāpy animittataḥ gārhapatyaṃ samāviśya tasmāt paśyāmy abhīkṣṇaśaḥ
english: 'I cannot behold or touch them without cause — and so, entering the householder's fire, I gaze upon them again and again.'

sanskrit: saṃspṛśann iva sarvās tāḥ śikhābhiḥ kāñcanaprabhāḥ paśyamānaś ca mumude gārhapatyaṃ samāśritaḥ
english: As if touching them all with his golden-bright flames, watching them as he dwelt in the domestic fire, he rejoiced.

sanskrit: niruṣya tatra suciram evaṃ vahnir vaśaṃ gataḥ manas tāsu vinikṣipya kāmayāno varāṅganāḥ
english: Having remained there for a very long time, Fire thus fell under the sway of desire, his mind cast upon those fair-limbed women whom he longed for.

sanskrit: kāmasaṃtaptahṛdayo dehatyāge suniścitaḥ alābhe brāhmaṇastrīṇām agnir vanam upāgataḥ
english: With his heart scorched by desire, fully resolved to abandon his body if he could not obtain the brahmin wives, Agni went into the forest.

sanskrit: svāhā taṃ dakṣaduhitā prathamaṃ kāmayat tadā sā tasya chidram anvaicchac cirāt prabhṛti bhāminī apramattasya devasya na cāpaśyad aninditā
english: Svāhā, the daughter of Dakṣa, had long desired him. That passionate woman had sought an opening in the vigilant god's conduct, but found none, blameless as she was in her search.

sanskrit: sā taṃ jñātvā yathāvat tu vahniṃ vanam upāgatam tattvataḥ kāmasaṃtaptaṃ cintayām āsa bhāminī
english: When she learned truly that Fire had gone into the forest truly scorched by desire, that passionate woman began to ponder a plan.

sanskrit: ahaṃ saptarṣipatnīnāṃ kṛtvā rūpāṇi pāvakam kāmayiṣyāmi kāmārtaṃ tāsāṃ rūpeṇa mohitam evaṃ kṛte prītir asya kāmāvāptiś ca me bhavet
english: 'Taking on the forms of the seven sages' wives, I shall approach the love-stricken Fire — bewildering him with their likenesses — and desire him. If I do this, his pleasure will be mine, and my longing too shall be fulfilled.'

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca śivā bhāryā tv aṅgirasaḥ śīlarūpaguṇānvitā tasyāḥ sā prathamaṃ rūpaṃ kṛtvā devī janādhipa jagāma pāvakābhyāśaṃ taṃ covāca varāṅganā
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Śiva, the wife of Aṅgiras, was endowed with virtue, beauty, and good qualities. Assuming her form first, the goddess approached the vicinity of Fire, O king, and that fair-limbed woman addressed him.

sanskrit: mām agne kāmasaṃtaptāṃ tvaṃ kāmayitum arhasi kariṣyasi na ced evaṃ mṛtāṃ mām upadhāraya
english: 'O Agni, I am tormented by love — you should desire me. If you do not do so, know that you shall see me dead.'

sanskrit: aham aṅgiraso bhāryā śivā nāma hutāśana sakhībhiḥ sahitā prāptā mantrayitvā viniścayam
english: 'I am Śiva, wife of Aṅgiras, O fire-devourer. I have come with my companions, having deliberated and made my resolve.'

sanskrit: agnir uvāca kathaṃ māṃ tvaṃ vijānīṣe kāmārtam itarāḥ katham yās tvayā kīrtitāḥ sarvāḥ saptarṣīṇāṃ priyāḥ striyaḥ
english: Agni said: 'How do you know that I am afflicted with desire? And how do the others — all the beloved wives of the seven sages whom you have named — know this?'

sanskrit: śivovāca asmākaṃ tvaṃ priyo nityaṃ bibhīmas tu vayaṃ tava tvaccittam iṅgitair jñātvā preṣitāsmi tavāntikam
english: Śiva said: 'You are ever dear to us, and we are ever in awe of you. Having read the signs of your heart, I have been sent to you.'

sanskrit: maithunāyeha saṃprāptā kāmaṃ prāptaṃ drutaṃ cara mātaro māṃ pratīkṣante gamiṣyāmi hutāśana
english: 'I have come here for union. Fulfil your desire quickly — my mothers await me and I must return, O fire-devourer.'

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tato 'gnir upayeme tāṃ śivāṃ prītimudāyutaḥ prītyā devī ca saṃyuktā śukraṃ jagrāha pāṇinā
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then Agni united with Śiva, filled with joy and delight. And when they joined, the goddess received his seed in her hand with love.

sanskrit: acintayan mamedaṃ ye rūpaṃ drakṣyanti kānane te brāhmaṇīnām anṛtaṃ doṣaṃ vakṣyanti pāvake
english: She thought: 'Those who see this form of mine in the forest will falsely attribute blame to the brahmin women in connection with Fire.'

sanskrit: tasmād etad rakṣyamāṇā garuḍī saṃbhavāmy aham vanān nirgamanaṃ caiva sukhaṃ mama bhaviṣyati
english: 'Therefore, to guard against this, I shall take the form of a Garudi — and my departure from the forest will thus be easy.'

sanskrit: suparṇī sā tadā bhūtvā nirjagāma mahāvanāt apaśyat parvataṃ śvetaṃ śarastambaiḥ susaṃvṛtam
english: Having become a Suparṇa-bird, she flew out of the great forest and beheld the white mountain well-covered with reed-thickets.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭīviṣaiḥ saptaśīrṣair guptaṃ bhogibhir adbhutaiḥ rakṣobhiś ca piśācaiś ca raudrair bhūtagaṇais tathā rākṣasībhiś ca saṃpūrṇam anekaiś ca mṛgadvijaiḥ
english: It was guarded by wondrous serpents of seven heads with poison in their gaze, and filled with rakshasas, pishacas, and fierce troops of spirits, as well as female rakshasas and multitudes of beasts and birds.

sanskrit: sā tatra sahasā gatvā śailapṛṣṭhaṃ sudurgamam prākṣipat kāñcane kuṇḍe śukraṃ sā tvaritā satī
english: She swiftly flew to the summit of that most inaccessible peak and, in haste, cast the seed into a golden vessel.

sanskrit: śiṣṭānām api sā devī saptarṣīṇāṃ mahātmanām patnīsarūpatāṃ kṛtvā kāmayām āsa pāvakam
english: That goddess also took on the likenesses of the remaining wives of those great-souled seven sages and, in each form, desired Fire.

sanskrit: divyarūpam arundhatyāḥ kartuṃ na śakitaṃ tayā tasyās tapaḥprabhāveṇa bhartṛśuśrūṣaṇena ca
english: She was unable, however, to assume the divine form of Arundhatī — for by the power of Arundhatī's austerities and her devoted service to her husband, that form remained beyond Svāhā's reach.

sanskrit: ṣaṭkṛtvas tat tu nikṣiptam agne retaḥ kurūttama tasmin kuṇḍe pratipadi kāminyā svāhayā tadā
english: Six times did that impassioned Svāhā cast Agni's seed into the golden vessel, O best of the Kurus, on the mountain's slope.

sanskrit: tat skannaṃ tejasā tatra saṃbhṛtaṃ janayat sutam ṛṣibhiḥ pūjitaṃ skannam anayat skandatāṃ tataḥ
english: That spilled seed, gathered together and charged with brilliance, there generated a son. The sages honoured him as 'Skanna' — the spilled — and from that came his name Skanda.

sanskrit: ṣaṭśirā dviguṇaśrotro dvādaśākṣibhujakramaḥ ekagrīvas tv ekakāyaḥ kumāraḥ samapadyata
english: The youth was born with six heads, twice the number of ears, twelve eyes arranged in order, twelve arms — and yet one neck and one body.

sanskrit: dvitīyāyām abhivyaktas tṛtīyāyāṃ śiśur babhau aṅgapratyaṅgasaṃbhūtaś caturthyām abhavad guhaḥ
english: On the second day he became manifest; on the third day the child shone forth; on the fourth, with all his limbs and sub-limbs fully formed, Guha came into being.

sanskrit: lohitābhreṇa mahatā saṃvṛtaḥ saha vidyutā lohitābhre sumahati bhāti sūrya ivoditaḥ
english: Wrapped in a great crimson cloud together with lightning, he blazed in that vast red cloud like the rising sun.

sanskrit: gṛhītaṃ tu dhanus tena vipulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam nyastaṃ yat tripuraghnena surārivinikṛntanam
english: He took up that great, hair-raising bow — the very bow set down by the Destroyer of the Three Cities — which cuts down the enemies of the gods.

sanskrit: tad gṛhītvā dhanuḥśreṣṭhaṃ nanāda balavāṃs tadā saṃmohayann ivemān sa trīṃl lokān sacarācarān
english: Taking up that foremost of bows, the powerful one then roared, as if bewildering these three worlds with all their moving and unmoving beings.

sanskrit: tasya taṃ ninadaṃ śrutvā mahāmeghaughanisvanam utpetatur mahānāgau citraś cairāvataś ca ha
english: Hearing his roar, which sounded like the thunder of great clouds, two great serpents leapt up — Citra and Airāvata.

sanskrit: tāv āpatantau saṃprekṣya sa bālārkasamadyutiḥ dvābhyāṃ gṛhītvā pāṇibhyāṃ śaktiṃ cānyena pāṇinā apareṇāgnidāyādas tāmracūḍaṃ bhujena saḥ
english: Seeing them rushing at him, he who blazed like the rising sun seized those two with two of his hands, held his spear in another hand, and with yet another arm clasped the crimson-crested cock, son of Agni's lineage.

sanskrit: mahākāyam upaśliṣṭaṃ kukkuṭaṃ balināṃ varam gṛhītvā vyanadad bhīmaṃ cikrīḍa ca mahābalaḥ
english: Gripping that great-bodied cock — best among the mighty — he roared fearfully and sported in his might.

sanskrit: dvābhyāṃ bhujābhyāṃ balavān gṛhītvā śaṅkham uttamam prādhmāpayata bhūtānāṃ trāsanaṃ balinām api
english: With two arms the powerful one seized a great conch and blew it — a sound that struck terror into all beings, even the mighty.

sanskrit: dvābhyāṃ bhujābhyām ākāśaṃ bahuśo nijaghāna saḥ krīḍan bhāti mahāsenas trīṃl lokān vadanaiḥ piban parvatāgre 'prameyātmā raśmimān udaye yathā
english: With two arms he struck the sky repeatedly; at play, the great commander shone brilliantly — drinking in the three worlds with his faces, unfathomable in nature, blazing on the mountain peak like the sun at its rising.

sanskrit: sa tasya parvatasyāgre niṣaṇṇo 'dbhutavikramaḥ vyalokayad ameyātmā mukhair nānāvidhair diśaḥ sa paśyan vividhān bhāvāṃś cakāra ninadaṃ punaḥ
english: Seated on the summit of that mountain, of wondrous valour, the immeasurable one surveyed the directions with his many faces; beholding the manifold aspects of existence, he roared once again.

sanskrit: tasya taṃ ninadaṃ śrutvā nyapatan bahudhā janāḥ bhītāś codvignamanasas tam eva śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ
english: Hearing his roar, people fell down in many places; frightened and their minds agitated, they fled to him alone for refuge.

sanskrit: ye tu taṃ saṃśritā devaṃ nānāvarṇās tadā janāḥ tān apy āhuḥ pāriṣadān brāhmaṇāḥ sumahābalān
english: Those people of various kinds who then took refuge in that god — those too came to be called his attendants, mighty brahmins among them.

sanskrit: sa tūtthāya mahābāhur upasāntvya ca tāñ janān dhanur vikṛṣya vyasṛjad bāṇāñ śvete mahāgirau
english: He, the mighty-armed, rose and comforted those people; then drawing his bow, he released arrows at the great white mountain.

sanskrit: bibheda sa śaraiḥ śailaṃ krauñcaṃ himavataḥ sutam tena haṃsāś ca gṛdhrāś ca meruṃ gacchanti parvatam
english: With his arrows he split Mount Krauñca, the son of Himavān — and through that cleft, geese and vultures travel to Mount Meru.

sanskrit: sa viśīrṇo 'patac chailo bhṛśam ārtasvarān ruvan tasmin nipatite tv anye neduḥ śailā bhṛśaṃ bhayāt
english: The mountain, shattered, fell crying out in great anguish; when it fell, other mountains cried out in great fear.

sanskrit: sa taṃ nādaṃ bhṛśārtānāṃ śrutvāpi balināṃ varaḥ na prāvyathad ameyātmā śaktim udyamya cānadat
english: Even hearing that cry of those in great distress, the best of the mighty was not troubled; unfathomable in soul, he raised his spear and roared.

sanskrit: sā tadā vipulā śaktiḥ kṣiptā tena mahātmanā bibheda śikharaṃ ghoraṃ śvetasya tarasā gireḥ
english: Then that great spear, hurled by that great-souled one, swiftly split the dreadful peak of the white mountain.

sanskrit: sa tenābhihato dīno giriḥ śveto 'calaiḥ saha utpapāta mahīṃ tyaktvā bhītas tasmān mahātmanaḥ
english: Struck by it, the wretched white mountain, together with its immovable companions, leapt up, abandoning the earth in fear of that great soul.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravyathitā bhūmir vyaśīryata samantataḥ ārtā skandaṃ samāsādya punar balavatī babhau
english: Then the earth was shaken and crumbled on all sides; in her distress she approached Skanda and became strong and firm again.

sanskrit: parvatāś ca namaskṛtya tam eva pṛthivīṃ gatāḥ athāyam abhajal lokaḥ skandaṃ śuklasya pañcamīm
english: The mountains too, bowing to him, returned to the earth. And from that time the world has celebrated the fifth bright day of Skanda's festivity.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ṛṣayas tu mahāghorān dṛṣṭvotpātān pṛthagvidhān akurvañ śāntim udvignā lokānāṃ lokabhāvanāḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: The sages, seeing various great and terrible portents, were troubled and performed peace-rites for the welfare of the worlds.

sanskrit: nivasanti vane ye tu tasmiṃś caitrarathe janāḥ te 'bruvann eṣa no 'narthaḥ pāvakenāhṛto mahān saṃgamya ṣaḍbhiḥ patnībhiḥ saptarṣīṇām iti sma ha
english: The people who dwelt in the forest of Citraratha said: 'This great calamity has been brought upon us by Fire, who united with the six wives of the seven sages.'

sanskrit: apare garuḍīm āhus tvayānartho 'yam āhṛtaḥ yair dṛṣṭā sā tadā devī tasyā rūpeṇa gacchatī na tu tat svāhayā karma kṛtaṃ jānāti vai janaḥ
english: Others said to the Garudi: 'This calamity was brought about by you' — for those who had seen the goddess moving in her form thought as much; but no one knew that the deed had been done by Svāhā.

sanskrit: suparṇī tu vacaḥ śrutvā mamāyaṃ tanayas tv iti upagamya śanaiḥ skandam āhāhaṃ jananī tava
english: The Suparṇa-bird, hearing those words, thought 'this child is mine.' She approached Skanda gently and said: 'I am your mother.'

sanskrit: atha saptarṣayaḥ śrutvā jātaṃ putraṃ mahaujasam tatyajuḥ ṣaṭ tadā patnīr vinā devīm arundhatīm
english: Then the seven sages, hearing that a son of great energy had been born, abandoned their six wives — all except the goddess Arundhatī.

sanskrit: ṣaḍbhir eva tadā jātam āhus tad vanavāsinaḥ saptarṣīn āha ca svāhā mama putro 'yam ity uta ahaṃ jāne naitad evam iti rājan punaḥ punaḥ
english: The forest-dwellers said that the child was born of those six alone. And Svāhā told the seven sages: 'This is my son.' But O king, they said again and again: 'We know that this is not so.'

sanskrit: viśvāmitras tu kṛtveṣṭiṃ saptarṣīṇāṃ mahāmuniḥ pāvakaṃ kāmasaṃtaptam adṛṣṭaḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nvagāt tat tena nikhilaṃ sarvam avabuddhaṃ yathātatham
english: The great sage Viśvāmitra, having performed a rite on behalf of the seven sages, had followed Fire unseen from behind while he was scorched with desire — and through this he had come to know everything in full, exactly as it happened.

sanskrit: viśvāmitras tu prathamaṃ kumāraṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ stavaṃ divyaṃ saṃpracakre mahāsenasya cāpi saḥ
english: Viśvāmitra was the first to take refuge in the youth and composed a divine hymn of praise to Mahāsena.

sanskrit: maṅgalāni ca sarvāṇi kaumārāṇi trayodaśa jātakarmādikās tasya kriyāś cakre mahāmuniḥ
english: The great sage also performed all the auspicious birth-rites and the thirteen Kaumara ceremonies, beginning with the birth-rite, for him.

sanskrit: ṣaḍvaktrasya tu māhātmyaṃ kukkuṭasya ca sādhanam śaktyā devyāḥ sādhanaṃ ca tathā pāriṣadām api
english: He also established the greatness of the six-faced one, the worship of the cock, the worship with the spear and of the goddess, and likewise the worship of his attendants.

sanskrit: viśvāmitraś cakāraitat karma lokahitāya vai tasmād ṛṣiḥ kumārasya viśvāmitro 'bhavat priyaḥ
english: Viśvāmitra performed all this for the benefit of the worlds, and thus the sage Viśvāmitra became dear to Kumāra.

sanskrit: anvajānāc ca svāhāyā rūpānyatvaṃ mahāmuniḥ abravīc ca munīn sarvān nāparādhyanti vai striyaḥ śrutvā tu tattvatas tasmāt te patnīḥ sarvato 'tyajan
english: The great sage confirmed the shape-changing of Svāhā and declared to all the sages: 'The women are not guilty.' Having heard the truth from him, the sages accordingly abandoned their wives completely.

sanskrit: skandaṃ śrutvā tato devā vāsavaṃ sahitābruvan aviṣahyabalaṃ skandaṃ jahi śakrāśu māciram
english: Then the gods, having heard of Skanda, spoke together to Vāsava: 'Skanda's power is unbearable — slay him, O Indra, quickly and without delay.'

sanskrit: yadi vā na nihaṃsy enam adyendro 'yaṃ bhaviṣyati trailokyaṃ saṃnigṛhyāsmāṃs tvāṃ ca śakra mahābalaḥ
english: 'And if you do not slay him today, this one will become Indra — the mighty one will subjugate the three worlds and you along with us, O Śakra.'

sanskrit: sa tān uvāca vyathito bālo 'yaṃ sumahābalaḥ sraṣṭāram api lokānāṃ yudhi vikramya nāśayet
english: He said to them, troubled: 'This child is of immense power — he could overpower and destroy even the creator of the worlds in battle.'

sanskrit: sarvās tv adyābhigacchantu skandaṃ lokasya mātaraḥ kāmavīryā ghnantu cainaṃ tathety uktvā ca tā yayuḥ
english: 'Let all the mothers of the world go to Skanda today and destroy him with their power of will and might.' Saying 'so be it,' they went.

sanskrit: tam apratibalaṃ dṛṣṭvā viṣaṇṇavadanās tu tāḥ aśakyo 'yaṃ vicintyaivaṃ tam eva śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ
english: But seeing him beyond all opposition, their faces fell; thinking 'this one cannot be overcome,' they too took refuge in him alone.

sanskrit: ūcuś cāpi tvam asmākaṃ putro 'smābhir dhṛtaṃ jagat abhinandasva naḥ sarvāḥ prasnutāḥ snehaviklavāḥ
english: And they said: 'You are our son; we sustain the world. Receive us all with joy — our breasts flow with milk, we are overcome with love.'

sanskrit: tāḥ saṃpūjya mahāsenaḥ kāmāṃś cāsāṃ pradāya saḥ apaśyad agnim āyāntaṃ pitaraṃ balināṃ balī
english: Mahāsena honoured them and granted their wishes; then the mighty one, mightiest of the strong, saw Fire coming toward him — his father.

sanskrit: sa tu saṃpūjitas tena saha mātṛgaṇena ha parivārya mahāsenaṃ rakṣamāṇaḥ sthitaḥ sthiram
english: Honoured by him, Fire, together with the host of mothers, encircled Mahāsena and stood firm, protecting him steadfastly.

sanskrit: sarvāsāṃ yā tu mātṝṇāṃ nārī krodhasamudbhavā dhātrī sā putravat skandaṃ śūlahastābhyarakṣata
english: Among all those mothers, the woman born of wrath — the wet-nurse — protected Skanda as a son, trident in hand.

sanskrit: lohitasyodadheḥ kanyā krūrā lohitabhojanā pariṣvajya mahāsenaṃ putravat paryarakṣata
english: The daughter of the crimson ocean — fierce, who feeds on blood — embraced Mahāsena and guarded him as a son.
